entries.title: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure and charters out tankers into October, sources say
entries.claimSummary: QatarEnergy extended force majeure for LNG supplies to several Asian buyers into mid-September.
extractedFacts: Force-majeure notices due to expire in August and early September were extended until mid-September.
Affected buyers include customers in South Korea, India and Bangladesh.
QatarEnergy continued leasing some LNG tankers through mid-October.
At least nine QELM/QET-controlled LNG carriers were sub-chartered to named third parties.

entries.title: No LNG tankers cross Strait of Hormuz since July 11 amid escalating US-Iran conflict
entries.claimSummary: Kpler reported no LNG carrier transits through Hormuz from July 11 through its July 18 observation.
extractedFacts: No LNG carriers transited the Strait of Hormuz after July 11 through the July 18 publication.
The last known LNG carrier transit occurred on July 11.
Kpler counted eight LNG carrier transits during May, not eight per day.
entries.carryReason: Firecrawl rechecked the exact Kpler article on 2026-07-31; no newer reviewed public LNG-specific transit observation was approved.

entries.title: Two Closed Corridors: Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb Both Effectively Shut to Tanker Traffic
entries.claimSummary: Windward reported the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed to commercial tanker traffic, with 6 total transits and zero tanker crossings on July 27.
extractedFacts: On July 27, 2026 the Strait recorded 6 total transits (3 inbound, 3 outbound), all via the northern corridor, with zero tanker crossings in either direction.
The closure is attributed to IRGC enforcement, sustained IRGC high-speed craft presence in the southern strait, and a northern-corridor bottleneck.
The count covers total vessel traffic and does not establish an LNG-specific transit count.
